newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina cuts soy, sunseed forecasts, ups maize.
newsitem.headline: Argentina cuts soy, sunseed forecasts, ups maize.

text.p: Argentina has cut its 1996/97 soybean and sunseed production forecasts and raised its maize estimates, the Agriculture Secretariat said Wednesday.

Soybean production forecasts were cut to 12.86 million tonnes from 13.5 million and sunseed forecasts were reduced to 5.17 million tonnes from 5.4 million. Maize output forecasts were raised to 14.41 million tonnes from 14.3 million.
Agriculture Secretary Felipe Sola told a news conference that drought had hit the soybean crop badly.

But he criticized recent private forecasts of soybean output of as low as 10.5 million tonnes, saying that they had overestimated the damage and that they were not properly based on fieldwork as were the official forecasts.
"There aren't any (reliable) private estimates about Argentine crops. There are people who give opinions based on the Secretariat's estimate," he said.
The Agriculture Secretariat has recently upgraded its crop estimate team, and incorporated analysis of satellite images.
About 16 percent of the soybean crop had been harvested by April 11, said Sola, adding that the drought damage might turn out to have been even worse than present evidence suggests.
He said 45 percent of maize had been harvested, and 86 percent of the sunflower crop.
The Secretariat raised its maize estimate after good early yields, he said.
